description: Two major Sramana traditions that emerged in ancient India during the 6th Century BC. They opposed complex Vedic rituals and the rigid caste system, emphasizing non-violence (Ahimsa), ethical living, and the path to salvation.

sections.title: Buddhism: Life and Teachings of Buddha
sections.description: Key life events of Gautam Buddha and the core philosophical principles of Buddhism.

key_concepts.explanation: The core teachings of Buddha: The world is full of sorrow (Dukkha), desire is the cause of sorrow (Samudaya), sorrow can be stopped (Nirodha), and there is a path leading to the cessation of sorrow (Magga).
The 'Middle Path' to achieve Nirvana, comprising Right View, Right Resolve, Right Speech, Right Action, Right Livelihood, Right Effort, Right Mindfulness, and Right Concentration.
The three pillars of the Buddhist faith: Buddha (The Enlightened One), Dhamma (The Teachings), and Sangha (The Monastic Order).

historical_events.significance: The Great Renunciation, where Gautam Buddha left his home and family in search of ultimate truth.
Buddha attained supreme enlightenment under a Bodhi Tree on the banks of the Niranjana River in Bodhgaya.
The 'Turning of the Wheel of Law', representing Buddha's first sermon delivered to five ascetics at the Deer Park in Sarnath.
The death of Gautam Buddha at the age of 80 in Kushinagar, marking his final release from the cycle of rebirth.

key_associations.extra_info: Born in 563 BC in Lumbini within the Shakya clan.
Sacred hemispherical monuments built over the bodily relics of Buddha.

sections.title: Buddhist Councils and Literature
sections.description: Chronology of Buddhist councils that codified literature and led to sectarian divisions.

historical_events.significance: Held at Rajagriha under the patronage of Ajatashatru. Resulted in the compilation of Sutta Pitaka and Vinaya Pitaka.
Held at Vaishali under the patronage of Kalashoka. Led to the first schism in the Buddhist order.
Held at Pataliputra under the patronage of Ashoka. The Abhidhamma Pitaka was compiled, completing the Tripitaka.
Held in Kundalavana, Kashmir under Kanishka. Buddhism officially split into Mahayana (idol worship) and Hinayana (traditional teachings) sects.

key_associations.extra_info: The largest of the Tripitakas, containing the religious discourses and main teachings of Buddha.
Contains the rules of monastic discipline and conduct for Buddhist monks and nuns.
Deals with the philosophical and psychological analysis of Buddhist doctrines.

sections.title: Jainism: Life and Teachings
sections.description: The tradition of Tirthankaras and the core philosophical doctrines established by Mahavira.

key_concepts.explanation: Spiritual teachers and saviors in Jainism. There were 24 Tirthankaras; Rishabhanatha was the first, and Parshvanatha was the 23rd.
The path to liberation consisting of Right Faith (Samyak Darshana), Right Knowledge (Samyak Jnana), and Right Conduct (Samyak Charitra).
Principles for monks: Non-violence (Ahimsa), Truth (Satya), Non-stealing (Asteya), Non-possession (Aparigraha), and Celibacy (Brahmacharya). Brahmacharya was added by Mahavira.
The Jain theory of relativity or pluralism, which states that ultimate truth and reality are complex and have multiple aspects.

historical_events.significance: Mahavira attained supreme knowledge under a Sal tree on the banks of the Rijupalika River in Jrimbhikagrama.

important_facts.fact: Vardhamana Mahavira was the 24th and last Tirthankara of Jainism.
Mahavira was born in 540 BC in Kundagrama, Vaishali into the Jnatrika Kshatriya clan.
He passed away (attained Nirvana) in 468 BC at the age of 72 in Pavapuri, near modern-day Rajgir, Bihar.

sections.title: Jain Councils, Sects, and Literature
sections.description: The division of Jainism into sects and the formalization of its sacred texts.

historical_events.significance: Held at Pataliputra under the leadership of Sthulabhadra. Resulted in the compilation of the 12 Angas.
Held at Vallabhi, Gujarat under Devardhi Kshamasramana. The final compilation of Jain literature took place here.

key_concepts.explanation: The 'White-clad' sect led by Sthulabhadra. They wear white garments and believe women can achieve liberation.
The 'Sky-clad' sect led by Bhadrabahu. They practice complete nudity as a sign of detachment and do not wear any clothes.

key_associations.extra_info: A core Jain text written in Sanskrit containing the biographies of the Jain Tirthankaras.
The primary sacred texts of Jainism, originally written in the Prakrit (Ardhamagadhi) language.
